title: Real-Time Audio Processing
service: RTLoop: a capture ring with a dBFS meter, SQLite latency traces in integer nanoseconds, a barge-in dialog, an asyncio stage pipeline, and a processing-graph planner

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Step 1 ring buffer; Concept: 20 ms frames (320 samples at 16 kHz) and code/main.rs FRAME_LEN = SAMPLE_RATE / 1000 * FRAME_MS; quiz core skills: samples per frame for any frame length and sample rate; quiz Q12 (a full deque(maxlen) drops the oldest samples silently); Concept: the ring prevents allocations in the hot path; code/main.py rms_dbfs with max(rms, 1e-10)
planted_bugs: RingBuffer.write splits a write at the wrap with capacity - start - 1: the last slot is never written and the wrapped samples land one slot late; the TypeError surfaces two calls later in meter.rms, on the None still in that slot

ms_to_samples divides before it multiplies (sample_rate // 1000 * ms, the formula of code/main.rs FRAME_LEN): exact at 16 and 48 kHz, but a 20 ms frame at 44.1 kHz comes out as 880 samples instead of 882 and every timestamp drifts
write makes room in a full ring with read(1) but never counts the evicted samples in dropped
every evicted sample costs a read(1), and read copies the whole ring, so a stalled loop makes the audio callback O(chunk x capacity)
parts.timing_assert: 100 callback writes of 20 ms into a full 1 s ring under 0.1 s (the starter takes 1.2 to 1.5 s; one-step eviction about 0.1 ms; the slowest legitimate fix, evicting through a two-slice read, 5 to 7 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: a full-scale sine reads -3.01 dBFS, which rules out a peak meter and AES17 sine-referenced dBFS; a muted mic reads exactly FLOOR_DBFS, which rules out -inf; frames are compared sample by sample, which rules out silencing the TypeError with zero-filled storage; int(sample_rate / 1000) * ms still truncates first and fails at 44.1 kHz; after a stall the first frame is at 300 ms and the newest samples come out, which rules out counting drops without moving the reader and timestamps that leave out the dropped samples

deviations: Part 1: the suggested list.pop(0) timing bug is replaced by eviction through a read that copies the whole ring. The starter's ring is the lesson's preallocated circular buffer with a wrap split, where pop(0) has no natural place. The cost appears only when the ring overflows, which is the real failure: the audio callback slows down exactly when the loop has stalled, and the lesson says the ring exists to keep allocations out of the hot path.

Part 1: the overwrite policy is planted as silent overflow (evicted samples not counted, quiz Q12). Keeping the oldest samples and reading past the writer (a lapped reader) are wrong-fix traps on the reference, caught by the quiz Q12 example, instead of extra planted bugs.

Part 2: no percentiles. The lesson's coderpad already has nearest-rank P50/P95, and latency metrics over an event stream belong to lesson 12; this part stays on exact storage, numbering and the budget boundary.

Part 3: time is passed into every call in integer nanoseconds, so the 100 ms rule and mid-chunk cuts are tested deterministically; the asyncio side of Step 4 (cancelling the TTS task) is tested in Part 4.

Part 4: no text wire format (see wire_format). The reference supervises with asyncio.wait and cancels each task once, because asyncio.gather returns as soon as the first child ends cancelled and a second cancel() interrupts the stage's own cleanup.
Part 5: adds the AEC far-end reference edge (a loop that is legal because it carries the previous frame) and a timing assertion against path enumeration.

code/main.rs: its FRAME_LEN formula (SAMPLE_RATE / 1000 * FRAME_MS, exact only when the rate divides by 1000) is the planted frame-length bug, shown at 44.1 kHz. The meter matches its rms_dbfs (20 * log10 of the RMS, floored at 1e-10); nothing in the pack contradicts its gain or FIR stage.
Part 1: the meter's digital-silence floor is a guard, not a planted bug, because Part 1 of 02 and 16 already plant a log of zero on silence.
